title: postfix ! before a member CALL compiles and runs: the allowance never ended at the call
notes: RETIRED REFUSAL, kept under its old filename so the COVERAGE.md row that cites it (§4.13) keeps resolving; the name records what this program used to be, not what it is. specification/failures.mdx §Refusal Conditions withdrew the five-condition placement walk this case certified, and DECISIONS.md §Typed failures records the withdrawal as the point of no return: `!` is accepted in any expression position, and three conditions refuse it — no enclosing Result channel, non-Result operand provenance, and an enclosing `catch`. WHY IT NOW PASSES, stated as a fact about the lowering rather than as a quotation: `lookup("ada")!` is evaluated unconditionally, exactly once, and with nothing effectful to its left in the statement, so the shipped early-return lowering hoists its guard to the front of the `const` and the emitted program calls `lookup`, checks, and then calls `.trim()` — the authored order, unchanged. The member CALL was never the thing that made this unsound; the old rule refused it because its walk stopped at the nearest statement through an allow-list of seven node kinds, and a call was not on the list. Its accepted twin postfix-bang-as-a-property-access-object-is-accepted is the identical program with `.length`, and the pair no longer records a distinction — both compile, and keeping both is what shows that.

xfail.reason: the fork still enforces the withdrawn statement-walk and refuses this program with SMITHERS1204 at the same authored position the retired expectation named. That is a FAIL-CLOSED divergence: the fork compiles nothing and runs nothing, so no marker here holds a fail-open. The reference moved when specification/failures.mdx §Refusal Conditions withdrew the placement rule (DECISIONS.md §Typed failures, 2026-08-30); `safeUnwrapPlacement` in compiler/forkbridge/lowering.go.txt is the fork's copy of the walk and has not been widened yet. MEASURED on both backends with `node conformance/runner/run.mjs --filter 02-unwrap-propagation`. The marker retires when the fork's placement walk is narrowed to the three residual conditions the reference now applies: a conditionally evaluated operand, a repeated loop header, and a propagation preceded by an unhoisted effect in the same statement.
xfail.doc: specification/failures.mdx §Refusal Conditions: 'The lowering emits a delegated suspension, which is an expression in every position and therefore preserves the authored evaluation order everywhere. Placement is unrestricted.'
